First of all, profit is revenue minus cost, or in our case, winnings minus cost. So, once we have found the expected winnings after twenty games, we need to subtract $10\cdot 20=200$ cents to account for the price of playing.

Now, let's find the expected winnings. For each play, the five coins have an equal chance of being dispensed, so each one has a probability of $\frac{1}{5}.$

Let's summarize this in a table. If $W$ is the amount of winnings (in cents) on a single game, and $f(w)$ is the probability mass function for $W,$ then we have the following:

| $f(w)$ | $\frac{1}{5}$ | $\frac{1}{5}$ | $\frac{1}{5}$ | $\frac{1}{5}$ | $\frac{1}{5}$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $w$ | $1$ | $5$ | $10$ | $25$ | $50$ |

The expected value of $W$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[W] & =1\cdot f(1)+5\cdot f(5)+10\cdot f(10)+25\cdot f(25)+50\cdot f(50) \\  & =1(\frac{1}{5})+5(\frac{1}{5})+10(\frac{1}{5})+25(\frac{1}{5})+50(\frac{1}{5}) \\  & =\frac{1}{5}+\frac{5}{5}+\frac{10}{5}+\frac{25}{5}+\frac{50}{5} \\  & =\frac{1+5+10+25+50}{5} \\  & =\frac{91}{5} \\  & =18.2.\end{aligned}
$$

This represents the expected winnings for a single game. So, the expected winnings for $20$ games is

$$
20\cdot \text{E}[W]=20\cdot 18.2=364.
$$

Now, subtracting the $200$ cents paid to play, we get that the expected profit (in cents) is

$$
E[p]=364-200=164.
$$
